task.title: Motor Bogie Maintenance — Periodic Inspection
task.shortdesc: Visual and clearance inspection procedure every 25,000 km.

section.title: 1. Purpose and scope
section.p: This procedure describes the checks the maintenance technician must perform on the motor bogie during the periodic inspection. The scope covers the primary suspension, the dampers and the axlebox fastening.
The operations described here must be carried out with the unit immobilized and locked out according to the facility's lock-out and tag-out procedure.
section.note: Do not enter the pit without confirming that the overhead line above the track is de-energized and earthed. Failure to do so may cause serious injury.

step.cmd: Visually inspect the primary suspension springs for cracks, deformation or corrosion.
Check the tightening torque of the axlebox fastening bolts with the torque wrench set to 120 Nm.
Measure the clearance between the damper plate and its support with the feeler gauge; the nominal value is 0.05 mm.
Check the condition of the elastic stops and the absence of oil leaks in the hydraulic dampers.
Record the readings obtained and compare them with the limit values in Table 2.

section.title: 4. Limit values and acceptance criteria
section.note: If the measured clearance exceeds 0.15 mm, replace the anti-friction bushing before returning the unit to service.

fig.title: Inspection points on the motor bogie (side view).

section.note: After replacing any suspension component, a test run is mandatory before returning the unit to commercial service.

section.title: 5. Records and traceability
section.p: All measurements must be recorded in the maintenance management system with the date, the unit identifier and the signature of the responsible technician.
